skill.name: git-pushing
skill.description: Stages all unignored changes, creates a Git commit, and pushes the current branch to origin with upstream tracking.
skill.summary: Commit and push all current Git changes through one scripted workflow.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The five static alerts are false positives because they identify code fences, an interpreter declaration, and a hardcoded Git branch lookup. The workflow still has medium operational risk because it stages every unignored change and pushes to origin without review or confirmation.

remediation.issue: Bulk staging can include sensitive or unrelated files.
remediation.suggestion: Show Git status and diff, stage selected paths, and require confirmation before committing and pushing.

remediation.issue: The script pushes the current branch to origin automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Display the resolved remote and branch, then require explicit confirmation before Git push.

finding_verdicts.reason: The substitution runs a fixed Git command and captures the current branch. No user-controlled text enters the command, and the result is quoted when used.
This line is only the Bash interpreter declaration. It does not construct a command from untrusted input or create an independent execution risk.
The snippet is a Markdown code-fence marker, not Ruby backtick execution. It only introduces a documented Bash command.
The snippet is a closing Markdown code fence. It is documentation syntax and cannot execute a shell command.
The snippet is a Markdown code-fence marker for the custom-message example. It is not executable Ruby or shell backtick syntax.

semantic_findings.title: Unreviewed Bulk Commit and Remote Push
semantic_findings.description: The script stages every unignored change, commits it, and pushes the current branch to origin without a diff review or confirmation. This can publish secrets, unrelated files, or unintended code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly runs git add, git commit, and git push in sequence. No review or confirmation step appears between these operations.

content.value_statement: Committing and publishing routine changes can require several Git commands. This skill stages all changes, creates one commit, and pushes the current branch.
actual_capabilities: Stages all unignored changes in the current repository.
Creates a commit using a supplied message.
Uses chore: update code when no message is supplied.
Pushes the branch to origin and sets upstream tracking.
limitations: It stages every unignored change and cannot select individual files.
It does not inspect diffs, run tests, or request confirmation.
It requires Git, an origin remote, and valid push credentials.
It stops when commits, hooks, authentication, or pushes fail.

use_cases.title: Publish a Small Fix
use_cases.description: Commit and push a completed fix from the current branch.

use_cases.title: Share Team Progress
use_cases.description: Push a reviewed feature branch with a specific conventional commit message.

use_cases.title: Automate Routine Updates
use_cases.description: Publish generated or maintenance changes through a consistent Git command sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Push Current Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Commit and push my current changes using the default message.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after reviewing a small set of repository changes.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Commit and push all current changes with the message fix: correct login redirect.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the commit purpose is already clear.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a Feature Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Push this feature branch with the message feat: add account export.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when publishing a completed feature to origin.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Reviewed Release Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Commit and push the reviewed release changes with the message chore: prepare version 2.4.0.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after validating all staged content, remote settings, and branch protections.

output_examples.input: Commit and push with the message fix: handle empty search results.
output_examples.output: All unignored changes were committed and the current branch was pushed to origin.

output_examples.input: Push my current work using the default message.
output_examples.output: The changes were committed as chore: update code and the branch was pushed with upstream tracking.

output_examples.input: Push these changes when origin rejects the branch.
output_examples.output: The push failed, and the script stopped with the Git error for manual resolution.

best_practices: Inspect Git status and the complete diff before invoking the skill.
Ensure .gitignore excludes credentials, local configuration, and generated files.
Provide a specific conventional commit message that describes the reviewed changes.
anti_patterns: Do not run the skill with unrelated or unreviewed worktree changes.
Do not use it when the current branch or origin remote is uncertain.
Do not expect it to resolve hooks, conflicts, authentication, or branch protection failures.

faq.question: Which files does the skill stage?
faq.answer: It stages every unignored change under the current repository.

faq.question: Can I provide a commit message?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply the complete message when requesting the commit and push.

faq.question: What message is used by default?
faq.answer: The script uses chore: update code when no message is provided.

faq.question: Which branch is pushed?
faq.answer: The script detects and pushes the currently checked-out branch.

faq.question: Which remote receives the push?
faq.answer: The script always pushes to the remote named origin.

faq.question: Does the skill run tests or review changes?
faq.answer: No. Review the diff and run required validation before invoking it.
